AIM.1.description: A strike is counted when the supervisor leaves S_HICCUP instead of when it enters it
AIM.1.reason: strike_level steps up only at the end of each cool-down, so hiccup_timer times the current cool-down from the old level, and latch_assert rises one whole cool-down late, after the converter has already restarted into the fault.

AIM.2.description: The clean-run cycle boundary is taken on the PWM rising edge instead of the falling edge
AIM.2.reason: clean_counter advances at the start of each switching cycle rather than at its end. strike_level is therefore cleared one PWM on-time early after a fault-free run, and a run that begins with PWM high counts one cycle fewer.

AIM.3.description: The latch test matches MAX_STRIKES-1 exactly instead of at-or-above, so a limit lowered below the count already reached is missed
AIM.3.reason: If the host lowers max_strikes below strike_level, the next hiccup entry does not assert latch_assert. The count wraps round its 2-bit range and the latch trips several hiccups late.

AIM.4.description: window_trip pauses the clean-run count instead of restarting it
AIM.4.before: else if (!run_active || window_trip) begin /  / clean_counter <= 0; /  / end /  / else if(pwm_fall) begin
AIM.4.after: else if (!run_active) begin /  / clean_counter <= 0; /  / end /  / else if(pwm_fall && !window_trip) begin
AIM.4.reason: A fault-window trip in the middle of S_RUN that does not cause a hiccup no longer restarts the streak. Cycles before the trip still count, so strike_level is cleared earlier than clean_run_target consecutive fault-free cycles.

AIM.5.description: The latch also trips on the strike level alone, outside a hiccup entry
AIM.5.after: end /  / else if (strike_level >= max_strikes) begin /  / latch_assert <= 1'b1; /  / end
AIM.5.reason: If the host lowers max_strikes to or below the strike count during S_RUN, latch_assert rises at once with no new hiccup. The specified behaviour is to trip only at the next hiccup entry at or past the limit.

AIM.6.description: strike_level is zeroed when the latch trips, instead of keeping the count for telemetry
AIM.6.after: if (strike_level >= max_strikes - 1'b1) begin / latch_assert <= 1'b1; / strike_level <= '0; / end
AIM.6.reason: After latch_assert rises, strike_level reads 0 instead of the count that tripped the latch, so the count is lost from telemetry while the converter stays latched.

AIM.7.description: The latch test compares the post-increment strike count against MAX_STRIKES-1, so the -1 for the pre-increment value is applied twice
AIM.7.reason: At the default max_strikes of 3, latch_assert rises on the second hiccup entry, when strike_level goes from 1 to 2, instead of the third. With max_strikes 2 it trips on the first hiccup.

AIM.8.description: The switching-cycle boundary is taken on both PWM edges, so each switching cycle counts twice toward the clean run
AIM.8.reason: In S_RUN, clean_counter reaches clean_run_target after half the intended number of switching cycles, so strike_level is cleared after about 0.5 s of fault-free running instead of 1 s.

AIM.9.description: The strike clear still waits for the old all-ones terminal count instead of clean_run_target, although the counter now saturates at the target
AIM.9.reason: At the default target, which is below all-ones, clean_counter stops at the target and never reaches all-ones. A strike earned by a hiccup is then never cleared, however long the run, and later isolated hiccups add up to latch_assert.
AIM.9.withdrawn: same output as AIM.17: the strike clear never fires, so strikes are never forgiven

judgements.reason: If clean_run_target is lowered below clean_counter while strikes are held, the original wraps and comes back to the target, clearing strike_level. The mutant saturates at all-ones and never equals the target, so line 140 never clears the strikes.

decisions.reason: differ only if clean_run_target is lowered below the running count; it changes only in S_OFF, where the counter is zero

AIM.10.description: The clean-run counter saturates at all-ones, the old fixed terminal, instead of holding at clean_run_target
AIM.10.reason: If the host lowers clean_run_target to a value below the current clean count while strikes are outstanding, the original counter wraps around and then clears strike_level when it reaches the new target. The mutant holds at all-ones and never matches, so strike_level stays non-zero until the next hiccup.

AIM.11.description: The strike clear waits for the next switching-cycle boundary after the clean run completes, instead of happening on the next clock
AIM.11.reason: In S_RUN with strikes outstanding, strike_level goes to zero one full PWM period after clean_counter reaches clean_run_target, not on the next clk. If S_RUN is left within that period, the clear never happens.

AIM.12.description: A completed clean run forgives one strike instead of clearing the whole count, and keeps doing so while the clean count stays saturated
AIM.12.reason: After a clean run in S_RUN with strike_level at 1, the clear branch fires every clock while the counter holds at the target. strike_level steps 0, 3, 2, 1 and so on, so the next hiccup gets the wrong cool-down and can trip latch_assert on its first entry.

AIM.13.description: A strike is counted on every change of hiccup_active, so both entering and leaving S_HICCUP add a strike
AIM.13.reason: Each hiccup now raises strike_level by two: one on entry and one when the cool-down ends and the supervisor goes back to S_SS. The cool-down level is wrong from the second hiccup on, and latch_assert trips after fewer hiccups than max_strikes allows.

AIM.14.description: strike_level is clamped at max_strikes-1, the deepest cool-down index, so the hiccup that trips the latch is not added to the count
AIM.14.reason: On the hiccup that asserts latch_assert, strike_level stays at max_strikes-1 instead of going to max_strikes. The final count read back for telemetry is one short every time the latch trips.

AIM.15.description: The latch is tested when the hiccup cool-down ends, on the post-increment count, instead of when the hiccup that reaches MAX_STRIKES begins
AIM.15.after: end /  / else if (hiccup_active_d & ~hiccup_active) begin /  / if (strike_level >= max_strikes) latch_assert <= 1'b1;
AIM.15.reason: On the hiccup that reaches max_strikes, latch_assert now rises only when hiccup_active falls at the end of the whole cool-down, not on the entry clock. Until then the supervisor sees no latch, and it moves from S_HICCUP to S_SS before shutting down.

AIM.16.description: The pre-increment -1 used by the latch test is copied into the clean-run clear, so strikes are forgiven one switching cycle before the clean run is complete
AIM.16.reason: strike_level goes back to zero one switching cycle earlier than clean_run_target cycles of S_RUN. If S_RUN is left exactly at target-1 cycles, the strikes are cleared although the original keeps them.

AIM.17.description: The clean-run counter saturates one cycle below clean_run_target, so it never reaches the value the strike clear waits for
AIM.17.reason: However long S_RUN stays fault-free, clean_counter stops at target-1, and the clear in the strike block (== clean_run_target) never fires. strike_level never returns to zero, so separate transients add up until latch_assert trips.

judgements.reason: When run_active is low and pwm_fall is high, the mutant skips the clear and increments clean_counter. For example, on the hiccup-entry edge a run streak survives into the hiccup and can later clear strikes the original would keep.

decisions.reason: shifts of one clock or one switching cycle: forgiveness on a 1 s window, or the latch 100 ns before the hiccup entry that sets it anyway

AIM.18.description: A switching-cycle boundary outranks the streak break, so a PWM fall on the clock S_RUN is left still counts as a clean cycle
AIM.18.reason: Say S_RUN is left (g_en dropped, say) on a clock with a PWM falling edge, and clean_counter is at target-1. The counter then reaches clean_run_target, and on the next clock strike_level is cleared although the clean run was cut short. The original clears the counter and keeps the strikes.

judgements.reason: pwm_sync_d stays frozen at its last S_RUN value. On the first edge of a new run, pwm_fall (line 94) compares pwm_sync with that stale level, not the previous clock's. This can add or drop a clean-cycle count at line 182 and shift the strike clear at line 140.

decisions.reason: shifts of one clock or one switching cycle: forgiveness on a 1 s window, or the latch 100 ns before the hiccup entry that sets it anyway

AIM.19.description: The PWM delay flop updates only in S_RUN, so on re-entry to S_RUN it compares against a stale PWM level from the previous run
AIM.19.reason: Suppose PWM was high when S_RUN was last left and is low on the first clock of the next S_RUN. pwm_fall then gives a false cycle boundary, so the clean run is counted one cycle long and strike_level is cleared one switching cycle early.

AIM.20.description: The clean-run streak is broken only on a switching-cycle boundary, so leaving S_RUN or a window trip between PWM falls leaves the saturated clean count standing
AIM.20.reason: After a long clean run (clean_counter at clean_run_target), a window_trip moves the supervisor to S_HICCUP, which has no switching-cycle boundary. The count survives the hiccup entry, so on the next clock strike_level drops back to 0 and the strike that hiccup earned is wiped. Repeated faults then never escalate the cool-down or reach latch_assert.

AIM.21.description: Leaving S_RUN only pauses the clean-run count instead of clearing it; only window_trip restarts the streak
AIM.21.before: else if (!run_active || window_trip) begin /  / clean_counter <= 0; /  / end /  / else if(pwm_fall) begin
AIM.21.after: else if (window_trip) begin /  / clean_counter <= 0; /  / end /  / else if(pwm_fall && run_active) begin
AIM.21.reason: Take a run that reaches clean_run_target and then leaves S_RUN through S_OFF (g_en low). The count stays at the target through S_OFF and S_SS. If a window_trip_SS hiccup follows, strike_level is cleared on the clock after its entry, so soft-start strikes never add up to latch_assert.

judgements.reason: latch_assert now sets on a window_trip with strike_level >= max_strikes-1, with no hiccup entry needed. It can rise earlier, or rise when no further hiccup ever happens, and it is a port.

decisions.reason: shifts of one clock or one switching cycle: forgiveness on a 1 s window, or the latch 100 ns before the hiccup entry that sets it anyway

AIM.22.description: The latch is armed on the run-window trip that leads to the final hiccup, one clock before that hiccup is entered
AIM.22.after: else if (window_trip && strike_level >= max_strikes - 1'b1) begin /  / latch_assert <= 1'b1; /  / end /  / else if (hiccup_entry) begin
AIM.22.reason: When strike_level is already max_strikes-1 and window_trip fires in S_RUN, latch_assert rises on that clock instead of one clock later on the S_HICCUP entry. The supervisor and the fault log therefore see the latch a cycle early.

AIM.23.description: The strike count saturates at MAX_STRIKES, so after the host lowers MAX_STRIKES below the count already reached, the latching hiccup is not counted
AIM.23.reason: Example: strike_level is 2 and the host writes MAX_STRIKES=1. The next hiccup still trips latch_assert, but strike_level stays at 2 instead of going to 3, so the strike_level reported for telemetry is one short.

AIM.24.description: A guard against the max_strikes-1 underflow is written with the wrong limit, so MAX_STRIKES=1 disables the latch
AIM.24.reason: With MAX_STRIKES written to 1 (the minimum reg_file allows), the first hiccup should assert latch_assert. Under this fault latch_assert never asserts, and strike_level keeps counting and wrapping on every later hiccup.

judgements.reason: If clean_run_target is lowered below clean_counter while strike_level is nonzero, the mutant freezes the counter above target and line 140 never fires. The original keeps counting, wraps and reaches the target, which clears strike_level.

decisions.reason: differ only if clean_run_target is lowered below the running count; it changes only in S_OFF, where the counter is zero

AIM.25.description: The clean-run counter holds at any count at or above clean_run_target, but the strike clear still waits for an exact match. So if the target is lowered below the running count, the counter freezes at a value that can never equal it.
AIM.25.reason: Suppose the host writes a CLEAN_RUN target below the clean count already reached while strikes are outstanding in S_RUN. The original counter keeps counting, wraps and then reaches the new target, so strike_level is cleared. The mutant holds the counter above the target, so strike_level is never cleared for the rest of that run.

AIM.26.description: A completed clean run sets the strike count back to one strike, treated wrongly as the base cool-down level, instead of clearing it to no strikes.
AIM.26.reason: After a fault-free run of clean_run_target cycles following a hiccup, strike_level reads 1 instead of 0. The next hiccup then gets the doubled cool-down index, and latch_assert trips one hiccup sooner than MAX_STRIKES allows.

AIM.27.description: The run-window trip is counted as a strike as well as the hiccup entry it causes, so every hiccup out of S_RUN adds two strikes
AIM.27.reason: window_trip is high on the last S_RUN clock and hiccup_entry fires on the next, so each overcurrent hiccup from S_RUN raises strike_level by 2 instead of 1. That lengthens the cool-down chosen by hiccup_timer, and with MAX_STRIKES=3 latch_assert trips on the second run hiccup instead of the third.

judgements.reason: clean_run_target can be lowered below the running count while strike_level is nonzero, so clean_counter > target is reachable. The mutant then clears strike_level at once; the original waits for the wrap back to exact equality.

decisions.reason: differ only if clean_run_target is lowered below the running count; it changes only in S_OFF, where the counter is zero

AIM.28.description: The strike clear fires when the clean count is at or above clean_run_target, while the clean-run counter itself saturates only on an exact match
AIM.28.reason: Say the host lowers clean_run_target in mid-run to below the clean count already reached. The original counter runs on past the new target and wraps before it matches, so strike_level stays nonzero for about 2**CLEAN_RUN_W more switching cycles. With this mutant strike_level drops to 0 on the next clock.

judgements.reason: On an edge where clean_counter == clean_run_target and window_trip is high, the original clears strike_level and the mutant does not. clean_counter is then zeroed (line 176), so the strikes stay.

decisions.reason: a window trip on the clock the clean run completes is never tested; the earned forgiveness must still clear the strikes

AIM.29.description: A window_trip on the clock the clean run completes cancels the strike forgiveness, although the run had already earned it
AIM.29.reason: Say window_trip is asserted on the first clock where clean_counter equals clean_run_target. The original zeroes strike_level on that edge. The mutant keeps the old count, so the hiccup that follows adds to it, and it can set latch_assert (for example with 2 strikes and max_strikes=3) where the original would only go to 1 strike.

AIM.30.description: The clean-run streak is broken by leaving S_RUN for any state except S_HICCUP, so a completed clean count survives into the cool-down
AIM.30.reason: Say hiccup_active rises as run_active falls after a completed clean run, with no window_trip on that clock. The clean count stays at clean_run_target through the cool-down, so one clock after the entry the clean branch zeroes the strike that hiccup just added. strike_level drops back to 0 during S_HICCUP, and repeated hiccups never set latch_assert.
AIM.30.withdrawn: part of AIM.21: the count survives only the exit into S_HICCUP, which AIM.21 also does; any test that kills AIM.21 on a hiccup exit kills it

AIM.31.description: Copy-paste slip in the delay-flop block: pwm_sync_d is loaded from hiccup_active instead of pwm_sync, so the switching-cycle boundary pwm_fall only fires around a hiccup exit and never while the converter is in S_RUN
AIM.31.reason: After any hiccup, the clean-run counter never advances in S_RUN, so strike_level stays non-zero however long the fault-free run lasts. Transients that are far apart then add up to latch_assert, when each should have been cleared after clean_run_target cycles.

AIM.32.description: Copy-paste slip in the delay-flop block: hiccup_active_d is loaded from pwm_sync instead of hiccup_active, so hiccup_entry is no longer a single pulse on entry into S_HICCUP
AIM.32.reason: In S_HICCUP the PWM is stopped, so pwm_sync stays low and hiccup_entry = hiccup_active & ~pwm_sync_prev is true on every clock of the cool-down. strike_level then goes up every clock instead of once per hiccup, and latch_assert trips during the first hiccup instead of the MAX_STRIKES-th.

AIM.33.description: The strike clear tries to anticipate the clean-run counter reaching its target on the switching-cycle boundary, instead of waiting for the counter to actually hold clean_run_target
AIM.33.reason: strike_level drops to zero one clock earlier than it should. It is also cleared when the final PWM fall of the run comes on the same clock as a window_trip or the exit from S_RUN: the counter is then cleared rather than completed, so the run never earned the forgiveness.

judgements.reason: A completed clean run (line 140) now also clears latch_assert. After latching, a later clean run in S_RUN would drop the latch_assert output, which only rst_n clears in the original.

decisions.reason: latch_assert must be cleared by reset alone, but no test runs a clean window after the latch; needs a clean run after latching with latch_assert checked to stay high

AIM.34.description: A completed clean run clears latch_assert along with the strike count, as though forgiveness reset the whole protection state, although latch_assert is meant to be set-only and cleared by rst_n alone
AIM.34.reason: After latch_assert has tripped, a later stretch of clean_run_target fault-free switching cycles with run_active high deasserts latch_assert at the port. This input sequence is allowed by the module's own interface, though at top level the supervisor's S_OFF lock-out keeps run_active low after a latch.

AIM.35.description: The latch test is moved out of the hiccup-entry branch to a later point in the cool-down. It compares the count after it has landed with MAX_STRIKES while hiccup_active is high, instead of testing the count about to land on the entry clock.
AIM.35.after: / end /  / else if (hiccup_active && strike_level >= max_strikes) begin / latch_assert <= 1'b1;
AIM.35.reason: On the hiccup that reaches MAX_STRIKES, latch_assert rises one clock late, so the supervisor stays in S_HICCUP one clock longer before it goes to S_OFF. Also, if the host lowers max_strikes to or below the current count during a cool-down, the latch trips in the middle of that cool-down instead of waiting for the next hiccup entry.
